title: Dispatch: ambiguity preflight before RNG; dedupe RulesAmbiguity type (attempt 6)
description:
Third review-response dispatch for eshyra-jw56 (PR #470). Two required findings.
Read `bd show eshyra-jw56` for the design history. Branch from the current tip of
`eshyra-jw56` (d37e7bd).

Worktree: `.worktrees/<this-bead-id>`, branch `<this-bead-id>`. Work only there.

## Fix 1 — an ambiguity failure must consume zero RNG

### The defect (confirmed by the supervisor, do not re-derive)

In `useItem` (`packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts`):

- line ~1884 `readItemState`
- line ~1886 `createInitialItemState(packRef, hit.record, { variantId, rng: input.rng, resolveTable })`
  — **consumes `input.rng`** for dice-derived economy maxima, spell-store
  `initialLevels`, and other initialization rolls
- line ~1908 `selectStateTransition(...)` — where `ItemStateAmbiguityError` throws

So a gated operation on a stateful item with no `item_state` row rolls dice
*before* it fails. The DB transaction rolls back; a seeded `Rng` does not. The
stream advances and replay diverges. Cube of Force does not expose this (its
gated transition is not reachable from `inactive`), but the contract now allows
a gate from any state including the initial one.

### Established facts (verified, build on these)

- `createInitialItemState` sets
  `machineState: String(obj(mechanics.stateMachine, ...).initial)`, so the
  machine's **declared `initial`** is exactly the state the later real selection
  will see. A preflight against `initial` cannot diverge from execution.
- Lazy init only happens under `if (stateful && state === undefined)`. When an
  `item_state` row exists, nothing between `readItemState` and
  `selectStateTransition` consumes RNG (`validateItemStateForRecord` takes only
  `{ resolveTable }`). **The RNG-before-gate window is exactly the lazy-init
  branch.**
- Operation-id resolution is at line ~1793 and the execution-readiness check at
  ~1840-1874 — both already before lazy init.

### Required implementation

Insert the ambiguity preflight **immediately before** the
`createInitialItemState` call, running only when that branch is about to be
taken. Use the machine's declared `initial` as the preflight source state.

Do **not** duplicate transition-matching logic. Extract the matching half of
`selectStateTransition` into a pure helper (e.g. `matchStateTransition`)
returning the selected raw transition/destination/outcome, and have both
`selectStateTransition` and the preflight call it. A second copy of the matching
rules that can drift is explicitly rejected by the reviewer.

The preflight must throw **only** `ItemStateAmbiguityError`. If the shared
matcher raises anything else (malformed machine, invalid destination, no
transition from that state, missing machineState), swallow it in the preflight
and let the normal path raise it in its existing position — that is what keeps
error precedence unchanged. The error keeps `ambiguityId`, `question`, all
declared `interpretationIds`, `owner: 'campaign-ruling'`, and pack ref +
operation id in the message.

**Do not** implement this by catching `ItemStateAmbiguityError` after
initialization. The RNG must never be invoked.

This placement preserves every precedence the reviewer listed — confirm each:
invalid operation ids (~1793) and readiness failures (~1840) still precede it;
persisted-state validation and `inert`/`nonmagical` lifecycle checks only apply
when a row exists, in which case the preflight does not run at all; non-stateful
items never lazily initialize; a machine-less stateful item makes the matcher
return undefined and the preflight a no-op.

### Required regression test

A schema-valid stateful magic item with **no** persisted `item_state` row, a
dice-defined economy maximum (so initialization would roll), and an
ambiguity-gated `via` self-transition **from the declared initial state**, plus
the ambiguity declaration with both interpretations. Drive it with an `Rng`
whose `nextInt` both counts calls and throws. Assert:

1. `ItemStateAmbiguityError` is thrown;
2. `ambiguityId`, `question`, `interpretationIds`, `owner` are all present;
3. **the RNG was called zero times**;
4. no `item_state` row exists afterward (query it directly);
5. inventory quantity, economies, and timers are unchanged.

Keep the existing already-initialized regression as-is. Add a positive companion
asserting an *unambiguous* operation on the same fixture still initializes lazily
and consumes RNG as expected — this is what stops the defect being "fixed" by
disabling initialization.

## Fix 2 — one canonical `RulesAmbiguity`

`packages/core/src/rules/rulesAmbiguities.ts` line 5 defines its own
`RulesAmbiguity`, duplicating the established contract at
`packages/core/src/rules/types.ts` line 97 (plus `RulesAmbiguitySource` and
`RulesAmbiguityInterpretation`). They are structurally identical today and can
drift. The drift is already live in the tree: the spell importer
(`s1SummoningSpecs.ts` line 1) imports the type from `types.js` while
`magicItemMechanics.ts` line 3 imports it from `rulesAmbiguities.js`.

Required:

- delete the duplicate interface from `rulesAmbiguities.ts` and
  `import type { RulesAmbiguity } from './types.js'` there (that module already
  imports `RulesPackError` from `./types.js`, so this adds no cycle);
- point `magicItemMechanics.ts` at the canonical `./types.js` type — it also
  already imports from `./types.js`;
- keep `types.ts` as the single definition site (it is the established public
  contract, re-exported from `internal.ts` lines 1048-1050); re-export from
  `rulesAmbiguities.ts` only if it genuinely helps, never redefine;
- use `import type` / `export type` throughout.

Add compile-time coverage that spell mechanics, magic-item mechanics, and the
public export all resolve to the same type — a mutual-assignability assertion in
a test file is enough (the repo does not currently use `expectTypeOf`). Confirm
`npm run typecheck` actually covers whatever file you put it in.

## Do not regress the completed review work

The Cube gate must stay exactly as it is: `ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset`,
both interpretations (`same-face-resets`, `different-face-only-resets`),
`canonicalResolution: null`, `status: 'engine-pending'`,
`owner: 'campaign-ruling'`, all five same-face transitions in `affects`, gated
transitions failing closed, the walker recognizing only
`{ kind: 'source-ambiguity', ambiguityId }`, a bare `ambiguityId` not counting as
a citation, `resetsDuration` requiring an operation-backed `via` and staying
self-transition-only, timer/condition uses rejected, one timer-bearing
transition per `from`/`to` pair, and preserved dice timers keeping their roll
without extra RNG. **Never reintroduce a provisional preserve-duration default.**

## Verification

Focused first: item-state execution and lazy init, item timers, magic-item
mechanics schema, generic ambiguity validation, Cube importer projection, and
the generated-pack membership/readiness assertions. Then, from the worktree
root: `npm ci`, `npm run verify:worktree`, and `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`.
(The repo is npm, not pnpm.) The generated pack must be unchanged by this bead —
if `records.json` moves, stop and report. Do not modify `package-lock.json`.

`git status --short` must be clean after committing. Do not push, do not open or
comment on a PR, do not merge. Never modify eshyra-jw56. Do not touch
`.worktrees/72ss-lx2j` or anything for eshyra-72ss / eshyra-lx2j.
